In this file is reported the code of local shrinkage and ridge regression Cross-Validation for Model 1

Loading libraries and data-set:

```{r}
library(caret)
library(Hmisc)
library(ggplot2)
library(MASS)
library(dplyr)
library(glmnet)
getHdata(gusto)
gusto.dat <- gusto

set.seed(4176340)

gusto.dat <- gusto[which(gusto$grpl %in% c(1,2,4) & gusto$grps %in% c(5,9,10,11)),]

#re-name the variables used in model 1
gusto.dat$HEI <- gusto.dat$height
gusto.dat$AGE <- gusto.dat$age
gusto.dat$WEI <- gusto.dat$weight
gusto.dat$PUL <- gusto.dat$pulse
gusto.dat$SYS <- gusto.dat$sysbp

```

Chosing the optimal threshold with Cross Validation which minimizes the MSE
```{r}
fold_k5 <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out= nrow(gusto.dat))) #index per fold

Cross_val_local_shrik <- function(neff) { 
  
  form1 <- WEI ~ HEI + AGE + PUL + SYS  #model 1
  
  mse <- rep(0,5)# empty MSE vector
  
  for(i in 1:5){
    train <- gusto.dat[fold_k5 != i, ] #fold partition
    test  <- gusto.dat[fold_k5 == i, ]
  
  #Training set shrinkage:
    
  #initialization:
    mod_OLS_base <- lm(formula = form1, data = train) #linear regression on train set
    X_ols <- model.matrix(~HEI+AGE+PUL+SYS, data= train) 
    XTX <- t(X_ols)%*%X_ols
    
    relvar_OLS <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols)) 
     for(j in 1:length(relvar_OLS)){
      relvar_OLS[j] <- (t(X_ols[j,])%*%solve(XTX)%*%X_ols[j,])}  # computation of 1/effective sample size linear regression on train set
    
    Z_ols      <- X_ols[,-1] #predictors without intercept
    n          <- nrow(Z_ols) 
    Z_shrink   <- Z_ols    #copy of the covariates that will be shrunk
    relvar_it  <- relvar_OLS #copy of hii = 1/ effective sample size
    z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink)  #average per predictor
    zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #covariates are centered
    X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink) #design matrix + intercept 
    iter       <- 0 
    maxiter    <- 1000
    dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  #distance is a function of the effective sample size
    diststart  <- dist  # initial distance saved
    max_dist <- n*1/neff-1  #maximum distance allowed i.e. minimum effective sample size threshold alloewd
    Cov <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink)
    
    
    ##while loop until all distances are below the threshold:
    while(max(dist) > max_dist & iter < maxiter){ 
  
   #compute the shrunk distance
      distshrink  <- dist
      distshrink[which(dist>max_dist)] <- max_dist #if dist > max_dist , dist is shrunk
  
  #compute shrinkage factor
      a           <- sqrt(distshrink/dist)
  
  
      azc         <- a*zc #  #shrink of the centered covariates
      Z_shrink    <- t(apply(X=azc, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #adding the mean 
  
      iter <- iter + 1  

      X_shrink   <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n), Z_shrink)  #adding the intercept to the shrunk predictors
   
      z_bar      <- colMeans(Z_shrink) # calculating the mean of the shrunk covariates 
  
      zc         <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #re-adding the mean computed after covariates shrinkage
  
  
      Cov        <- ginv(t(X_shrink)%*%X_shrink) #re-compute the shrunk XTX
  
      relvar_it  <- diag(X_shrink %*% Cov %*% t(X_shrink))  #re-compute  the inverse of XTX with shrunk Cov 
  
      n_eff      <- 1/relvar_it #re-compute effective sample size (inverse of leverage hii)
  
      dist       <- n*relvar_it - 1  #re-compute the distances
      }


  train_shrunk <- data.frame("WEI" = train$weight) 
  train_shrunk <- cbind(train_shrunk, Z_shrink)
  mod_train_shrink <- lm(formula = form1, data = train_shrunk ) #fit the model on the shrunk training covariates
  

  
  #test set shrinkage:
  X_ols_test <- model.matrix(~HEI+AGE+PUL+SYS, data= test) 
  relvar_OLS_test <- numeric(length = nrow(X_ols_test))  
  
  for(k in 1:length(relvar_OLS_test)){                #computing inverse of effective sample size on test set
    relvar_OLS_test[k] <- (t(X_ols_test[k,])%*%Cov%*%X_ols_test[k,])}
  
  n.test <- nrow(X_ols_test)
  
  test_distance <- n*relvar_OLS_test-1 #test set distances
  
  
  distshrink_test <- pmin(test_distance, max_dist)  #selecting only distances < maxdist or distance will be = maxdist
  
  a_test <-  sqrt(distshrink_test / test_distance)  #computing shrinkage factor for subjects in the test set


  Z_ols_test   <- X_ols_test[,-1] # new patients (test set) without intercept
  
  Z_shrink_test <- Z_ols_test 
  
  relvar_it_test <- relvar_OLS_test

  zc_test        <- t(apply(X=Z_shrink_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x-z_bar})) #center the covariates of the test set using the average of the shrunk training set covariates
  
  azc_test <-zc_test*a_test#  shrinking the new patients  (test set) covariates 
  
  Z_shrink_test    <- t(apply(X=azc_test, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(x){x + z_bar})) #adding the mean 
  
  X_shrink_test <- cbind(icpt=rep(1,n.test), Z_shrink_test) #shrunk test set predictors

  #MSE:
  
  test_shrunk <- data.frame("WEI" = test$weight) #observed test set response variable weight
  test_shrunk <- cbind(test_shrunk, Z_shrink_test) 

  pred <- predict(mod_train_shrink, newdata = test_shrunk) #compute predictions using the test se
  
  mse[i] <-  mean((test$weight- pred)^2)} #compute the MSE
  
  return(mean(mse)) 
  }
```

CV search for the optimal threshold which minimizes the MSE:
```{r}
grid_neff <- c(0,30,40,50,70) #grid of candidates thresholds
mse_values <- sapply(grid_neff, function(x) { Cross_val_local_shrik(neff = x) }) #applying the CV function over the grid
results <- data.frame( neff = grid_neff, MSE = mse_values ) 
best_grid <- results[which.min(results$MSE), ] 
results  
best_grid #Optimal threshold for model 1 is "neff"=50
```


Global shrinkage: ridge regression CV

```{r}

x <- model.matrix( ~ HEI + AGE + PUL + SYS, gusto.dat)[,-1] 
y <- gusto.dat$WEI
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet( x, y, alpha = 0, lambda =  c(1, 0.5,0.1,0.05,0.02,0.01, 0), keep = T,foldid = fold_k5  )  #cv using the same folds as local shrinkage

cv_ridge$lambda.min # 0.1

# computing un-weighted mean of folds' MSE:

j <- which(cv_ridge$lambda == 0.1)

pred <- cv_ridge$fit.preval[, j] #predictions 

# MSE per fold
mse_fold <- sapply(1:5, function(i) { #MSE per fold
  idx <- fold_k5 == i
  mean((y[idx] - pred[idx])^2)
})

mean(mse_fold) #mean MSE
```
